title: Petra and the Promise
premise: Rosalind Almeida built her career orchestrating other people's perfect days after her own love story ended in silence — ten years of unsigned letters she never sent, and a wedding she walked away from. When Julian Voss, the man those letters were meant for, moves in next door as the new owner of the crumbling estate she's been hired to restore for a society wedding, the past stops staying past. As the commission that could save her business collides with the truth of who he is and why he left, Rosalind must choose between protecting the life she rebuilt and risking it on a promise made a decade ago. In the end, she lets the letters be read aloud, loses the contract, and finds that love, finally in the present tense, is the only inheritance that matters.
about_author: Kestrel Coldharbour is the pen name of a former event coordinator who spent seven years watching promises being made and quietly collecting the ones that broke. She writes from a coastal cottage where the post arrives late, which she considers a professional advantage.

chapters.title: The Last Tense
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She flawlessly executes a stranger's wedding while privately insisting love belongs in the past tense. Establishes her cynicism, her thriving business, and the locked box of unsent letters she keeps under her floorboards. Emotional beat: controlled grief disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: The Commission of the Year
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A lucrative, career-saving contract lands: restore Hollowmere Estate and stage the wedding of a wealthy socialite's daughter. Rosalind accepts despite the estate's reputation for ruin. Beat: hope with an undertow of dread.

chapters.title: The New Neighbor
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Moving trucks arrive at the cottage next door. Through her window she glimpses a man carrying a crate of books and feels an unwelcome jolt of recognition. Beat: the past knocking.

chapters.title: Julian
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. He has returned to England after a decade abroad, drawn by an inheritance he never wanted — Hollowmere itself. He notices the woman next door and something about her posture haunts him. Beat: restlessness seeking a shape.

chapters.title: Hollowmere's Bones
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. First walkthrough of the estate: peeling ballroom, overgrown rose court, a chapel with a broken bell. She catalogs damage the way she catalogs feelings. Beat: beauty under decay, mirroring herself.

chapters.title: Coffee, Carefully Measured
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Julian knocks with borrowed-ladder diplomacy. Their first conversation is polite, guarded, electric. She deflects; he persists gently. Beat: two people recognizing each other while pretending not to.

chapters.title: The Client's Daughter
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Bride-to-be Camille Ashworth is kind but steamrolled by her mother, Vivienne, whose demands grow impossible. Rosalind recognizes the pattern of a woman being married off to a legacy. Beat: empathy sharpening into unease.

chapters.title: What the Letters Were
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, with flashbacks. Ten years ago she wrote Julian a letter a month for a year after he left — and never sent one. The flashback reveals the quarrel and the silence that followed. Beat: the wound given a face.

chapters.title: A Ladder Against the Wall
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. He begins helping with the estate restoration unasked, and their collaboration finds an easy rhythm. He tells himself his interest is neighborly. Beat: denial wearing work gloves.

chapters.title: The Rose Court
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Clearing the overgrown roses, they unearth a stone bench with initials carved into it — initials that are theirs. Neither explains how. Beat: the past surfacing literally.

chapters.title: Camille's Confession
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. She admits to Rosalind she doesn't love her fiancé; the marriage is Vivienne's design. She begs Rosalind, of all people, to understand. Beat: Rosalind's cynicism cracked by a mirror.

chapters.title: Rain on the Glasshouse
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Trapped by a storm in the estate's glasshouse, he and Rosalind talk until the rain stops — about everything except the thing between them. Beat: intimacy achieved through evasion.

chapters.title: Vivienne's Terms
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Vivienne threatens to pull the contract over a scheduling dispute, revealing how fragile Rosalind's financial rescue is. Beat: duty tightening its grip.

chapters.title: The Unsent Year
chapters.summary: Julian's POV, with flashbacks. He reveals to a friend that he once received nothing from Rosalind after he left — no letter, no goodbye — and it taught him she never cared. Dramatic irony lands. Beat: the tragedy of crossed silences.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. After a successful venue milestone, wine on her porch, a moment that nearly becomes a kiss — interrupted by a phone call from Vivienne. Beat: longing interrupted by obligation.

chapters.title: The Floorboard Box
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Repairing Rosalind's sagging floor while she's out, Julian finds the box of unsent letters addressed to him. He reads the first one. Beat: devastation and revelation in a single act.

chapters.title: What He Read
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. He reads all twelve letters through the night, learning the truth of the decade-old quarrel: he was told a lie by his brother, and she was told he'd asked her not to write. Beat: grief reorganized as fury and hope.

chapters.title: The Confrontation That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Julian returns the box without explanation, saying only, 'You wrote to me.' Rosalind, humiliated, slams the door on the conversation. Beat: pride as self-defense.

chapters.title: Camille Runs
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. Camille disappears two weeks before the wedding, leaving a note and chaos. Vivienne blames Rosalind and threatens ruin, legal and professional. Beat: stakes made material.

chapters.title: Finding Camille
chapters.summary: Rosalind and Julian's alternating POV. They trace Camille to a coastal inn where she's working a kitchen shift, finally breathing. Rosalind, instead of dragging her back, listens. Beat: Rosalind choosing truth over contract for the first time.

chapters.title: The Terms of My Heart
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Julian tells her the whole truth: his brother's lie, the intercepted letters, the decade of believing himself unloved. Rosalind cannot speak; the box on the table says it for her. Beat: the past tense finally broken.

chapters.title: Present Tense
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. First kiss, first honest night, first morning. Julian dares to imagine a future; Rosalind is already calculating what Vivienne's retaliation will cost. Beat: joy shadowed by the clock.

chapters.title: Vivienne's Leverage
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Vivienne discovers the romance and the Camille cover-up, and offers a devil's trade: end it publicly, or Rosalind's business, reputation, and references die with the wedding. Beat: the choice made explicit.

chapters.title: The Career That Saved Everything
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, with flashbacks to the bankruptcy she rebuilt herself from. She weighs the business — her identity, her survival — against Julian. Beat: the theme of inheritance turned inward.

chapters.title: Julian's Offer
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian offers to sell Hollowmere and fund her fresh start anywhere, asking her to choose him openly. Rosalind, terrified of being saved rather than choosing, refuses. Beat: love offered, pride mistaken for duty.

chapters.title: The Cold Week
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. They orbit each other in silence. She signs Vivienne's amended terms in all but name; the wedding proceeds with her name attached and her heart removed. Beat: the lowest ebb.

chapters.title: Camille Returns
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. Camille comes back on her own terms to face her mother, and publicly refuses the marriage at the rehearsal dinner. Vivienne's fury redirects entirely onto Rosalind. Beat: the younger woman's courage indicting the older woman's fear.

chapters.title: The Broken Bell
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian restores the chapel bell alone, an act of stubborn faith. He leaves a thirteenth letter in Rosalind's mailbox — the first he has ever written her. Beat: the correspondence reversed.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Letter
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She reads his letter: not a plea, but an account of what her words meant to a man who thought himself unloved, and an invitation to read hers aloud, if she ever wants to. Beat: the decision crystallizing.

chapters.title: What Rosalind Decides
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She drafts her resignation from the Ashworth commission, hands shaking, and realizes the career saved her life but cannot be permitted to own it. Beat: the choice made, terror and clarity together.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Rosalind and Julian's alternating POV. In the restored rose court, she reads the twelve letters aloud to him, one per month of the year she wrote them. He answers each with the truth he lived. Beat: catharsis; the climax's emotional peak.

chapters.title: Vivienne's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV. Stripped of her daughter's wedding and her leverage, Vivienne is confronted by Camille and, unexpectedly, by her own memory of a love she sacrificed to duty. Beat: the antagonist given a human floor.

chapters.title: The Wedding That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The Ashworth wedding is cancelled; the industry gossip mill turns. Rosalind loses the contract, half her clients, and none of herself. Beat: the cost paid in full and found survivable.

chapters.title: Hollowmere Sold
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian sells the estate — to Camille, who will make it something new. He keeps only the bell. Beat: inheritance refused and transformed.

chapters.title: Small Hours
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The quiet aftermath: a rebuilt floorboard, a shared kitchen, learning each other in the present tense without a deadline. Beat: tenderness after the storm.

chapters.title: The Business, Rebuilt Small
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind restarts as a planner of tiny, honest ceremonies — including, at Camille's request, Camille's small wedding to no one's design but her own. Beat: vocation redeemed.

chapters.title: The Bell Rings
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian hangs the bell at the cottage between their homes. Its first ring is for no occasion at all. Beat: joy as a daily practice, not an event.

chapters.title: A Promise, Kept Late
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Ten years and one week after the quarrel, Julian asks the question the letters were always circling. Rosalind answers in the present tense. Beat: the promise fulfilled.

chapters.title: The Smallest Wedding
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, brief rotating sections. Their wedding at Hollowmere's rose court: Camille as witness, Vivienne invited and changed, the bell ringing. Beat: the theme resolved — love and duty reconciled by choosing honestly.

chapters.title: Letters, Ongoing
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, years later. She still writes him letters, but now she sends them. The final image: the mailbox between two cottages, always full. Beat: love as a continuing correspondence rather than a concluded contract.
